reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly demonstrates that adding 50 at.% Pt to an FeCoNiMnCu film and applying RTA yields an L10 phase with a three-orders-of-magnitude coercivity increase, supporting the core premises. However, the hypothesis proposes FeCoNi (without MnCu) as the base alloy, which is a minor extrapolation not directly tested in E1, and the mechanism details (spin–orbit coupling, domain wall pinning) are inferred rather than explicitly measured in the cited work.
premises: Pt addition (~50 at.%) to an fcc alloy can induce L10 ordering after RTA
L10 ordering dramatically increases magnetic anisotropy
Increased magnetic anisotropy raises coercive field by orders of magnitude
The mechanism involves enhanced spin–orbit coupling and structural anisotropy from Pt-induced ordering
The predicted effect applies to sputtered thin films on Si/SiO2 with RTA
